story_theme_en: A garden has 38 flower pots. The gardener plants 17 new flowers in pots. Later, 9 flowers are picked by visitors. How many flower pots have flowers now?
helper_tip_en: First add the new flower pots, then subtract the pots whose flowers were picked. Use a bar model to track the changes.
think_story_en: Garden starts with 38 pots. Plants 17 more: 38 + 17 = 55 pots with flowers. Then 9 are picked: 55 - 9 = 46 pots still have flowers.

visual_blocks.title: Try It!
visual_blocks.question: A library has 42 books on Monday. They add 28 new books on Tuesday. On Wednesday, 15 books are borrowed. How many books are left?

data.question: A library has 42 books on Monday. They add 28 new books on Tuesday. On Wednesday, 15 books are borrowed. How many books are left?

explanation_steps_en: Read the word problem carefully. Identify what we start with, what is added, and what is taken away.
Draw a bar model to visualize the parts and the whole.
First add the new items to the original amount.
Then subtract the items that are removed.
Check your answer to make sure it makes sense.

worked_examples_en.question_en: A park has 30 benches. Workers add 20 more benches. Later, 15 benches are moved to another park. How many benches are left?
A factory makes 45 toys. They make 25 more the next day. Then 30 are shipped to stores. How many are left?

common_mistakes_en: Forgetting to do operations in the correct order (the order events happen).
Making mistakes in column addition and subtraction.
Not checking if the answer makes sense in the story context.
hints_en: Always solve in the order the events happen.
Use a bar model to organize the information.

test_bank_en.q: A bakery has 60 cakes. They bake 25 more. Then 35 are sold. How many cakes are left?
A fish tank has 34 fish. The pet store adds 26 more fish. Then 18 fish are sold. How many fish are in the tank?

explanation_en: Mixed operations problems combine addition and subtraction. Follow the order of events in the story. First add what comes in, then subtract what goes out. A bar model helps organize the information.
